entries.name: Notes on modules of finite injective dimension
entries.abstract: Motivated by Bass' conjecture, we study finitely generated modules of finite injective dimension and the additional constraints they impose on the ambient ring. Beyond ensuring the Cohen--Macaulay property, the presence of such modules enforces further conditions on the ring, including reducedness, normality, being an integral domain, and various singularity conditions such as complete intersection, Gorenstein, and beyond. This continues to detect non-singularity as well. We also address the reflexivity (and also torsionlessness) of modules with finite injective dimension and show that this forces the ring to be quasi-normal. In the same vein, we investigate the injective dimension of tensor products and endomorphism rings. Finally, we study the behavior of R when high syzygies of ksurject onto a non-zero R-module of finite injective dimension.

entries.name: A polyptych of multi-centered deformation spaces
entries.abstract: Extending Verdier's deformation space to the normal cone of a closed subscheme and Rost's double deformation space of a pair of nested closed subschemes, we introduce a notion of deformation spaces attached to chains of immersions of arbitrary lengths $n$. One main result, which builds on the formalism of multi-centered dilatations of schemes, is the existence of so-called panelization isomorphisms, which produce under suitable regularity conditions several canonical isomorphisms between a given deformation space of length $n$ and some deformation spaces of smaller lengths. Having these panelization isomorphisms also allows to give geometric descriptions of the strata -- certain restrictions of special interest -- of deformation spaces.

entries.name: Settling the no-$(k+1)$-in-line problem when $k$ is not small
entries.abstract: What is the maximum number of points that can be selected from an $n\times n$ square lattice so that no $k+1$ of them are collinear? This was asked more than $100$ years ago for $k=2$ and it remained wide open ever since. In this paper, we prove the exact answer is $kn$, provided that $ n\ge k\ge C\log n$ for an absolute constant $C<20$. The proof relies on carefully constructed block-uniform random bipartite graphs and concentration inequalities.

entries.name: Unlikely intersections in Shimura varieties and beyond: a survey
entries.abstract: The aim of this note is to provide a concise introduction to so-called problems of unlikely intersections for (pure) Shimura varieties and to review the current state-of-the-art. In the process, we will touch upon more general settings and some of the results in those contexts.

entries.name: Embedding lattices of quasivarieties of periodic groups into lattices of additively idempotent semiring varieties: An algebraic proof
entries.abstract: A general result by Jackson (Flat algebras and the translation of universal Horn logic to equational logic, J. Symb. Log. 73(1) (2008) 90--128) implies that the lattice of all quasivarieties of groups of exponent dividing $n$ embeds into the lattice $L(\mathbf{Sr}_n)$ of all varieties of additively idempotent semirings whose multiplicative semigroups are unions of groups of exponent dividing $n$; the image of this embedding is an interval in $L(\mathbf{Sr}_n)$. We provide a new, direct, and purely algebraic proof of these facts and present a new identity basis for the top variety of the interval. In addition, we obtain new information about the lattice $L(\mathbf{Sr}_n)$, demonstrating that the properties of the lattice for $n\ge 3$ differ drastically from those previously known when $n=1$ or $2$.

entries.name: A marking graph for finite-type Artin groups
entries.abstract: Clean markings on surfaces were a key component in Masur and Minsky's hierarchy machinery, which proved to be a powerful tool in the study of mapping class groups. We construct a marking graph for irreducible finite-type Artin groups which is quasi-isometric to the group modulo its center, i.e., an element of $A_Γ/Z(A_Γ)$ is determined up to finite error by its action on one of our markings. To construct this graph, we construct suitable collections of transverse parabolic subgroups which extend the maximal simplices of the complex of irreducible parabolic subgroups to analogues of clean markings, and we define natural analogues of elementary moves.

entries.name: Survival of the fittest Cox model: Pivotal variable selection for time-to-event data
entries.abstract: We revisit Cox's proportional hazards model to improve variable selection in survival analysis. A square-root transformation of the partial likelihood renders the selection of the regularization parameter asymptotically pivotal: the baseline hazard and the censoring rate cancel exactly, and the way censoring is spread over time only enters through a bounded correction of order $1/\log n$. Using martingale residuals, we compute this penalty level by Monte Carlo without reordering the design matrix. The resulting criterion borrows from information criteria such as BIC and from penalized regression methods such as the lasso, taking the best of both. On simulated and real data, our method substantially improves upon state-of-the-art approaches used daily.

entries.name: Oort's conjecture on automorphisms of generic supersingular abelian varieties
entries.abstract: We prove Oort's conjecture that generically on the supersingular locus of the moduli space of principally polarized abelian varieties of genus g and in characteristic p, the automorphism group of the universal principally polarized abelian variety consists only of $\pm 1$, unless g=2, 3 or 4 and p=2. On the way, we provide an explicit description of the a=1-locus in the Rapoport-Zink space of principally polarized supersingular p-divisible groups of any dimension g. We also prove analogous results for generic automorphism groups on moduli spaces of supersingular p-divisible groups with and without polarization.

entries.name: Benders Cut Filtering for Affine Potential-Based Flow Problems with Robustness Scenarios and Topology Switching
entries.abstract: Many large-scale optimization problems decompose into a master problem and scenario subproblems. Benders decomposition exploits this structure by iteratively solving the subproblems and adding constraints, called Benders cuts, to the master problem. We study Benders cut filtering: given a set of Benders cuts produced in one iteration, which subset should be added to the master problem? Adding all generated cuts can cause rapid master problem growth, whereas retaining fewer cuts may require more Benders iterations. To our knowledge, few prior works have studied this question for Benders cuts. Classical cut filtering techniques require modification because Benders cuts enforce constraints omitted from the master problem, whereas conventional cutting planes are optional inequalities that strengthen the relaxation. We propose violation-based filtering, diversity-based filtering via k-medoids clustering on cosine distances, and a hybrid that selects a most-violated cut per cluster. We compare these strategies with no filtering, random filtering, and our adaptation of SCIP's hybrid cut selector on an affine potential-based flow problem with topology switching and robustness scenarios. On instances solved by all configurations, our hybrid approach reduces the shifted geometric mean solve time by about 45% compared to no filtering, and by 39% compared to our adaptation of SCIP's hybrid cut selector. While violation-based filtering achieves a similar runtime, the hybrid approach requires about 17% fewer callback rounds. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of Benders cut filtering on this problem class and motivate evaluation in other domains.

entries.name: Gradient Regularized Newton Boosting Trees with Global Convergence
entries.abstract: Gradient Boosting Decision Trees (GBDTs) dominate tabular machine learning, with modern implementations like XGBoost, LightGBM, and CatBoost being based on Newton boosting: a second-order descent step in the space of decision trees. Despite its empirical success, the global convergence of Newton boosting is poorly understood compared to first-order boosting. In this paper, we introduce Restricted Newton Descent, a framework for convex optimization with Newton's method on Hilbert spaces with inexact iterates, based on the concepts of cosine angle and weak gradient edge. Within this framework, we recover Newton boosting with GBDTs and classical finite-dimensional theory as special cases. We first prove that vanilla Newton boosting achieves a linear rate of convergence for smooth, strongly convex losses that satisfy a Hessian-dominance condition. To handle general convex losses with Lipschitz Hessians, we extend a recent gradient regularized Newton scheme to the restricted weak learner setting, establishing the first global $\mathcal{O}(\frac{1}{k^2})$ convergence rate for second-order GBDTs. This scheme minimally modifies the classical algorithm by introducing an adaptive $\ell_2$-regularization term proportional to the square root of the gradient norm at each iteration. In numerical experiments, we show that this scheme converges while vanilla Newton boosting may diverge.

entries.name: Shape theory for condensed anima
entries.abstract: We give different perspectives on the notion of shape for condensed anima. We prove that it recovers more classical notions of shape not only for all locally compact Hausdorff but also locally contractible spaces. These recovering statements imply and extend comparison results on sheaf and condensed cohomology by Clausen-Scholze and Haine. Another homotopy-theoretical direction for condensed anima are their condensed homotopy groups. Connected to this, we give a description of the underlying topological group functor on condensed groups via quasi-topological groups.

entries.name: Minkowskian open/closed conformal field theory possibly without vacuum: the Cardy case
entries.abstract: For any conformal net, not necessarily rational, we construct the associated Cardy-type conformal field theory on the Minkowski spacetimes $(\mathbb R/2π\mathbb Z)\times\mathbb R$ for closed strings and $[0,π]\times\mathbb R$ for open strings within the framework of algebraic quantum field theory. In addition to verifying some of their basic properties, we prove three forms of Haag duality for multi-double-cones and boundary intervals, interpreted respectively as the Minkowskian versions of modular invariance, the Cardy consistency condition, and the Morita equivalence of boundary field algebras.

entries.name: A Game-Theoretic Characterization of Feedback Capability for Fully Coupled Vector-Valued Nonparametric Systems
entries.abstract: We study feedback stabilization for the discrete-time system $x_{t+1}=f(x_t)+u_t+w_{t+1}$ in $\mathbb{R}^d$ with unknown $f$ and arbitrary bounded disturbances. For scalar plants, the sharp feedback capability threshold under generalized Lipschitz uncertainty is $\frac{3}{2}+\sqrt{2}$. We treat fully coupled vector-valued systems, where scalar order and interval recursion are unavailable and coupling precludes a coordinatewise reduction. We introduce a response-history escape game whose adversarial objective requires a finite envelope and an unbounded state radius. Borel determinacy, invariance under a change of finite initial history, and slope monotonicity define a game value $Γ_d$. One causal feedback law stabilizes every plant in the uncertainty class against every bounded disturbance sequence whenever $L<Γ_d$. At every $L\geΓ_d$, each causal feedback law and each initial state admit a globally $Γ_d$-Lipschitz plant whose state norms tend to infinity with zero disturbances. Thus stabilization is possible exactly below the critical value. We also prove $Γ_d=1+(\log d)/(2d)+O((\log\log d)/d)$, with explicit coefficients in bounds on both sides of the remainder. Explicit finite-dimensional bounds give $Γ_d>1$ in every dimension and $Γ_2\ge 7/5$. A nearest-neighbor law achieves the planar guarantee. The values are nonincreasing in dimension, and comparison with the scalar theory yields $Γ_1=\frac{3}{2}+\sqrt{2}$.

entries.name: On the Maximum Number of Vertices that Belong to Every Metric Basis
entries.abstract: Resolving sets of graphs have been widely studied since their introduction in the 1970's by Slater and, independently, by Harary and Melter. The minimum cardinality of a resolving set of a graph $G$ is called the metric dimension of $G$ and is denoted by $\dim(G)$. In this paper, we concentrate on the existence of vertices in a graph $G$ that belong to all metric bases of $G$, i.e. resolving sets of cardinality $\dim(G)$. Such vertices are called basis forced vertices, and we denote the number of them by $\mathrm{bf}(G)$. We show that $\mathrm{bf}(G)\le 2/3(n-\dim(G)-1)$ for any connected nontrivial graph $G$ of order $n$. In addition, we show that this bound can be attained. Furthermore, it also implies that $\mathrm{bf}(G)\le 2/5(n-1)$ holds for any nontrivial connected graph $G$. This result answers a question posed by Bagheri \emph{et al.} in 2016. Moreover, we provide a complete realization of the parameters $n$, $\dim(G)$ and $\mathrm{bf}(G) \ge 1$ within the previous bounds. We consider some extremal cases related to basis forced vertices in a graph, in particular, we give a full characterization of the graphs with $\mathrm{bf}(G) = 2$ and $\dim(G) = n-4$.

entries.name: Randomized Block Davidson Eigensolvers for Plane-Wave Density-Functional Theory
entries.abstract: Iterative diagonalization is the dominant cost of plane-wave density-functional theory (DFT), with search-space orthogonalization scaling particularly quickly with problem size and the number of target states. We present a randomized block Davidson-type eigensolver that replaces Euclidean orthogonalization with randomized Gram-Schmidt in a sketched inner product, requiring only a single pass over the basis while keeping its conditioning bounded independently of the input vectors. This modification changes only the Rayleigh-Ritz step, which becomes a definite generalized Hermitian eigenproblem. Ritz extraction remains exact, preserving true Ritz pairs and the interlacing property that makes each band energy an upper bound on the true one. The method is implemented in mixed precision for CPUs and GPUs from a single Julia code, interfaces matrix-free with DFTK, and is released in the open-source RandESC library. On sparse test problems with a fixed number of eigenpairs, the sketched solver overtakes its deterministic counterpart beyond matrix dimensions of about $2\times 10^4$ and is $25\%$ faster at $5\times 10^5$. In full self-consistent field DFT calculations, the benefits of sketching depend on the application case. With standard pseudopotentials and plane-wave cutoffs, efficiency gains are limited. As the number of requested states grows with system size, orthogonalization savings are offset by the generalized eigenproblem. However, some highly accurate pseudopotentals require larger cutoffs, and in this regime, the randomized solver is measurably better by $6\%$ overall. Its relative efficiency also improves as simulated systems get larger.

entries.name: Agnostic Smoothed Online Regression with Adversarial Responses
entries.abstract: We study smoothed online prediction with bounded adversarial responses. This widely studied framework bridges i.i.d. sampling and adversarial covariate selection through a smoothness parameter $\textsf{C}_{\textsf{cov}}$, which bounds conditional covariate densities relative to a fixed, unknown base measure. We propose Hedge-Cover, an information-theoretic algorithm that achieves sublinear regret $\widetilde{O}(\sqrt{\text{Pdim}(\mathcal{F}) \textsf{C}_{\textsf{cov}} T})$ for function classes with bounded pseudo-dimension. The algorithm aggregates a carefully constructed family of experts using Hedge, with a prior that links regret to the number of disagreements between a consistent selector and a target function. We bound this number by exploiting covariate smoothness. This answers an open problem posed in \cite{blanchard2025agnostic} on the minimax optimal adaptive regret of the smoothed online regression problem. We establish a matching lower bound for the class of linear predictors. The main intricacy of the lower bound lies in explicitly constructing a challenging sequential covariate distribution supported on mutually orthogonal hyperplanes. This construction may be of independent technical interest. Finally, we revisit the well-specified setting and quantify the effect of response noise. For conditionally $ν^2$-subGaussian responses, we extend the existing lower bound under realizable responses by showing that the minimax expected regret is $Ω((1\vee ν)\sqrt{(\textsf{C}_{\textsf{cov}}-1)dT})$ for a function class of VC dimension $d$. A corresponding upper bound for ERM matches this dependence on $ν$.

entries.name: Exclusion vs Noncolliding Dynamics in Markov Processes
entries.abstract: Let $(ξ_t)_{t \geq 0}$ be a continuous-time Markov process taking values in a countable state space $E$. We consider $k$ copies of $ξ$ started from distinct positions, and write $X = (X_t)_{t \geq 0}$ for the resulting process of configurations in $E^k$. We compare two forms of interaction between the particles: the first is conditioning the particles to never collide (noncolliding dynamics), and the second is simply switching off any jumps that would cause two particles to occupy the same position (exclusion dynamics). We show under mild conditions on the tail probabilities of the collision time that the dynamics are related by an explicit exponential martingale change of measure of one another. This generalises a recent result in the integrable probability literature relating TASEP on the ring to asymmetric walkers conditioned to never collide.

entries.name: Inter-Categorical Subobject Analysis
entries.abstract: We introduce a systematic way to use the subobject functor on any category to set up a framework for generalized topological and measure-theoretic notions and inferences. Concretely, we develop two connected calculi: 1. a fourfold calculus derived from notions of smallness and density that generalizes, among other things, topological density and measure-theoretic negligibility, 2. a twofold calculus that generalizes topological and measure-theoretic inference procedures. The resulting theory is distinguished in that it is inter-categorical in character: its definitions can be applied not just to describe smallness and density of subobjects in any category and classify morphisms by how they handle them, but also functors and natural transformations by how they transform them, somewhat like the theory of limits but with a simple and intuitive conceptual meaning that applies to each incarnation. We provide examples of these notions from many areas of mathematics and outline their unfolding throughout category theory as we add assumptions that bring them closer to classical settings, which we complete by generalizing the topological duality of open and closed subsets and outlining a possible framework for a categorical measure theory. Central to this interaction is the subobject 2-functor and the 2-category of upward-bounded preorders, so in the last part of the text we provide a study of their function. Concretely we derive representation theorems for this 2-functor and 2-category and a conjecture about how to generalize these theorems to n-categories.

entries.name: Digraph Laplacian spectra: The 2005 polygon conjecture fails for all orders above four
entries.abstract: Let $Λ_n$ be the set of all eigenvalues of standardized Laplacian matrices of order $n$, equivalently, of stochastic $n\times n$ matrices with off-diagonal entries at most $\frac1n$. In 2005, a polygon $S_n\subseteqΛ_n$ was constructed, and it was conjectured that $Λ_n=S_n$; this holds for $n\le3$. We show that the conjecture fails for every $n\ge5$. The vertices of $S_n$ are eigenvalues of circulant Laplacians built from powers of the directed $n$-cycle. To first order, no perturbation of these circulants moves such an eigenvalue out of $S_n$; however, adding chords with nonconstant weights moves it along an edge of $S_n$ to first order and, with an explicit coefficient, beyond the supporting line of this edge to second order. Consequently, every edge of $S_n$ not incident to $0$ or $1$ contains interior points of $Λ_n$, except possibly, for even $n$, the two horizontal edges, whereas the four edges incident to $0$ or $1$ lie on $\partialΛ_n$. For $n=4$, whose only other edges are horizontal, the question has recently been settled, $Λ_4=S_4$, by computer-assisted proofs of D. Z. Liu and L. Marshall; Liu also proved that $Λ_n$ is not convex for $n\ge5$. We certify an explicit weighted counterexample for $n=5$, lying only $1.5\cdot10^{-3}$ outside $S_5$, and an unweighted one for $n=7$: the directed $6$-cycle with a duplicated vertex. Its eigenvalue outside $S_7$ is also an eigenvalue of the two-chord digraph that ends the above perturbation; for the analogous digraphs of order $n$, the excess is asymptotic to $\frac{π^2}{2n^4}$. We also observe that $S_n$ is a zonotope, describe $Λ_n$ in terms of eigenvectors, and prove that $S_m\subseteq S_n$ whenever $m\mid n$.

entries.name: Seven ordered points and the nonexistence of arithmetic ball quotient compactifications
entries.abstract: We prove that the ordered GIT quotient of seven points on $\mathbb P^1$ with equal weights is not isomorphic to the Baily--Borel compactification of any arithmetic complex ball quotient. Together with our companion paper and the known positive examples, this determines the equal weight case for every $n\ge6$: such a realization exists precisely for $n=6,8$. The lattice and the algebraic isomorphism are unrestricted, and torsion and divisorial ramification are allowed. The proof combines arithmetic reductions with identities involving Chern classes of fixed subvarieties and intersection inequalities for nef divisors on the GIT quotient. The final comparison includes all fixed components and requires no bound on the degree of an individual fixed curve.

entries.name: The second closed geodesic on Finsler manifolds with $\mathbb{Z}_2$ fundamental group
entries.abstract: Let $(M, F)$ be a compact bumpy Finsler manifold with $π_1(M)=\mathbb{Z}_2$, we prove that there exist at least two distinct non-contractible closed geodesics on $(M, F)$.

entries.name: Identifying codes of Archimedean grids
entries.abstract: An identifying code of a graph is a dominating set $C$ such that the sets $N[v]\cap C$ are pairwise distinct. The minimum density of an identifying code has been studied extensively for several infinite grids. It is known to be $1/4$ for the triangular grid and $7/20$ for the square grid, whereas for the hexagonal grid the problem is still open, between $5/12$ and $53/126$. These three grids are the regular members of the family of the eleven Archimedean grids. In this paper, we start a systematic study of identifying codes in this family. We determine the minimum density for five of the nine Archimedean grids for which it was not known: it is $2/3$ for the truncated hexagonal grid, $3/7$ for the truncated square grid, and $1/3$ for the trihexagonal (kagome) grid, the elongated triangular grid and the snub hexagonal grid. All lower bounds are proved by the discharging method. For the three remaining non-regular Archimedean grids, we also obtain some bounds: the minimum density lies between $3/7$ and $13/30$ for the truncated trihexagonal grid, between $1/3$ and $11/30$ for the rhombitrihexagonal grid, and between $2/7$ and $9/28$ for the snub square grid. As a by-product, we prove that every identifying code of a cubic graph with the slow growth property in which every vertex lies on exactly one triangle (resp. $4$-cycle) has density at least $2/3$ (resp. $3/7$).

entries.name: Voevodsky's motives and zeroth slice of motivic sphere
entries.abstract: Let $S$ be a noetherian scheme of finite Krull dimension and let $R$ be a commutative ring in which the positive residue characteristics of $S$ are invertible. We identify Voevodsky's stable Nisnevich category of motives with $R$-coefficients with the category of modules over the zeroth slice of the motivic sphere with derived $R$-coefficients. The equivalence takes the free module on a smooth $S$-scheme to its motive with transfers and commutes with pullback and extension of coefficients. It applies to singular and nonreduced schemes and to mixed-characteristic bases. The main geometric input is the base change stability of Voevodsky's motivic Eilenberg--MacLane spectrum $HR_S$. We prove this using permutation quotients of tori, families of relative cycles and arithmetic power homotopies. The identification over fields and the reconstruction theorem of Cisinski--Déglise then give the module equivalence.

entries.name: Converse symplectic interlacing via low-rank singular value perturbations
entries.abstract: The symplectic interlacing theorem states that the symplectic spectrum of a $2n \times 2n$ real symmetric positive definite matrix satisfies a $2k$-step interlacing relation with the symplectic spectrum of every $2(n-k) \times 2(n-k)$ $s$-principal submatrix. We prove the converse in this paper. More precisely, given a global symplectic spectrum of size $n$ and a local symplectic spectrum of size $n-k$ satisfying the $2k$-step interlacing inequalities, we construct a $2n \times 2n$ real symmetric positive definite matrix having the prescribed global symplectic spectrum and a $2(n-k) \times 2(n-k)$ $s$-principal submatrix of it having the prescribed local symplectic spectrum. A novelty of our method is building a connection between the $s$-principal submatrix problem and low-rank singular value perturbations. We also provide an algorithm to determine a positive definite matrix that realizes the given global and local symplectic spectra. In the context of the Gaussian quantum marginal problem, our result implies that the symplectic interlacing inequalities are not merely necessary conditions on Gaussian marginals, but are also the complete spectral compatibility conditions for the global-versus-local-mode marginal problem.

entries.name: Newtonian Dynamics in Metric Spaces
entries.abstract: We develop a variational framework for second-order, frictionless (Newtonian) dynamics in metric spaces, extending the metric theory of curves of maximal slope from gradient flows to evolutions with inertia. The construction rests on three pillars, mirroring the first-order theory. First, we introduce a class of second-order absolutely continuous curves, characterized by a geometric--variational inequality on families of tangent geodesics, and define a metric notion of acceleration. Second, we define curves of Newtonian motion as the curves achieving equality in an energy inequality involving an upper gradient--Hessian pair, which in Hilbert spaces is equivalent to Newton's equation $\ddotγ= -\nabla E(γ)$. Third, we propose a two-step predictor--corrector minimizing movement scheme and show that its discrete interpolants satisfy approximate versions of these inequalities. Under extendability and interceptor conditions on geodesics---which are satisfied, for instance, by geodesically uniformly complete, locally compact spaces with curvature bounded below---and under suitable regularity assumptions on the energy, we prove that the scheme converges, up to subsequences, to a curve of Newtonian motion. As an illustration, we recover the linear wave equation as a curve of Newtonian motion driven by the Dirichlet energy. This paper is complemented by the companion paper [Fornasier, Klemenc, Scagliotti, "A Lions Lift Framework for Gradient and Newtonian Evolutions in Wasserstein spaces"], which specifies and adapts the results to the Wasserstein metric space $(\mathcal{P}_2,W_2)$ through Lions lift, which explains Vlasov equations as Newtonian flows on spaces of probability measures.

entries.name: Funnel MPC for port-Hamiltonian systems
entries.abstract: Port-Hamiltonian systems are an energy-based modelling formalism, that has strong ties to the physical models and allows interconnection of systems. Funnel MPC, a Model Predictive Control (MPC) scheme, allows for output tracking with prescribed error bounds. Earlier works focused on systems with stable internal dynamics, which typically excludes port-Hamiltonian systems. We introduce a modified stage cost design that takes into account the port-Hamiltonian structure of the system and allows deactivation of the funnel cost. We show initial and recursive feasibility for a class of port-Hamiltonian systems with relative degree one including unstable internal dynamics.

entries.name: Asymptotic efficiency of tests for quantum statistical models
entries.abstract: In classical statistics, local asymptotic normality provides a general framework for characterizing optimal testing power and constructing asymptotically efficient procedures. Extending this framework to quantum statistical models introduces additional challenges arising from the noncommutativity of observables and the need to optimize over quantum measurements. In this paper, we develop a theory of asymptotic efficiency for quantum hypothesis testing using quantum local asymptotic normality and the asymptotic representation theorem. We establish sharp nuisance-maximin power bounds for one-sided tests and two-sided tests within the unbiased class by reducing the corresponding classical--quantum Gaussian shift experiments to classical testing problems. This reduction is justified through a quantum Hunt--Stein argument that accommodates both commuting and noncommuting Gaussian coordinates. Under suitable asymptotic invariance conditions, the resulting bounds transfer to the original quantum experiments and are attained by scalar symmetric logarithmic derivative tests. We further develop a two-stage adaptive construction that achieves the same local asymptotic power without knowledge of the reference parameter. As an application, we study testing of smooth spectral functionals of quantum states. We compare scalar symmetric logarithmic derivative tests with the weak Schur sampling plug-in test and with optimally weighted linear statistics of its fluctuations. This comparison distinguishes loss from the plug-in weighting from a gap between the best such spectral statistic and the scalar score procedure. We characterize equality of the corresponding variances and illustrate the two gaps through explicit examples.

entries.name: Removable forests in $k$-connected and $k$-edge-connected graphs
entries.abstract: We prove the forest conjecture of Clay and Jordán: Let $k\ge1$ be an integer and let $F$ be a forest with $m$ vertices and $e$ edges. If a $k$-connected graph $G$ has minimum degree at least $\max\{k+e,m-1\}$, then it contains a copy of $F$ whose edge deletion preserves $k$-connectivity. We also prove the $k$-edge-connectivity version.

entries.name: Anytime-valid goodness-of-fit test by $e$-spacings
entries.abstract: To perform an anytime-valid goodness-of-fit test, we propose spacing-based \(e\)-processes that control the type-I error rate under arbitrary stopping rules. Based on the maximum spacing of order statistics, we construct spacing-based \(e\)-processes for nonparametrically testing distribution. The resulting procedures are simple and computationally efficient, and are power-consistent. We call them $e$-spacing tests. This approach is especially powerful in detecting localized discrepancy between the data-generating density and the null density. Under mild conditions, the logarithm of the proposed \(e\)-process is asymptotically equivalent to that of the oracle-optimal \(e\)-process. We further generalize the construction from maximal spacing to maximum spacing set in the form of the \(1/k\) fraction of the largest \(m\)th order spacings, as a measure of the lower-level set of density. It boosts power under more global discrepancy from the null. Furthermore, we propose a greedy predictable scheme, via argmax or softmax rules, to combine multiple $e$-spacing testing strategies. We prove that it optimally tunes the $e$-spacing test. The proposed approach is readily generalizable to multivariate testing via a coordinate-wise Rosenblatt-transform. Simulation studies demonstrate that the proposed methods perform favorably relative to the considered anytime-valid competitors as well as various types of multiple test-adjusted Kolmogorov--Smirnov tests.

entries.name: Quasi-orthogonality is a geometric property
entries.abstract: Quasi-orthogonality is one of the key ingredients for proofs of optimal convergence rates for adaptive mesh refinement methods (Carstensen, Feischl, Page, and Praetorius, arXiv:1312.1171). The work of Feischl (arXiv:2008.12198) proposed a relaxed quasi-orthogonality that follows directly from the inf-sup stability of the underlying problem discretization. The proof uses an intricate connection to the stability of $LU$-factorization of matrices. Recently, Gantumur (arXiv:2609.16265) presented a vastly simplified argument based solely on Hilbert space arguments. Building on this idea, we show that quasi-orthogonality is a purely geometric property of a set of points. This property is checked for a large class of Petrov-Galerkin methods for monotone, non-linear equations.

entries.name: Determination of the unbounded potential of the Robin Laplacian from fixed-time boundary measurements of time-fractional diffusion-wave equations
entries.abstract: We consider the time-fractional diffusion-wave equation $\partial_t^ρu - Δu + q u = 0$ in a bounded domain $Ω\subset \RR^n$, $n \geq 3$, where $\partial_t^ρ$ is the Caputo derivative of arbitrary order $ρ\in (0,2)$. This framework covers in a unified way the sub-diffusive case $ρ\in (0,1)$, the classical heat equation $ρ= 1$, and the super-diffusive case $ρ\in (1,2)$. The real-valued potential $q$ is only assumed to lie in $L^{n/2}(Ω)$, and the equation is endowed with zero initial conditions and a non-homogeneous Robin boundary condition, whose coefficient is allowed to be unbounded as well. The boundary excitations are supported in an arbitrary open subset $Γ_0$ of the boundary, and the trace of the solution is measured, at one fixed time, on another open subset $Γ_1$. We prove that the corresponding Robin-to-Dirichlet map uniquely determines the boundary spectral data of the underlying Robin Laplacian on $Γ_0 \cup Γ_1$, provided that $Γ_0$ and $Γ_1$ overlap. When $Γ_0 \cup Γ_1$ is the whole boundary, we deduce that $q$ is uniquely determined by this map in every dimension $n \geq 3$, the critical case $q \in L^{3/2}(Ω)$ in dimension three being included. The proof combines analytic continuation in the time variable, the Laplace transform and an identification of the poles and residues of meromorphic functions. The potential is then recovered from the boundary spectral data through an elliptic Robin-to-Dirichlet map, an integral identity, and complex geometric optics solutions.

entries.name: Time-independent equivalent matrix representation for time-domain boundary element analysis of large-scale 3D acoustic problems
entries.abstract: This paper proposes a time-independent equivalent matrix representation for large-scale three-dimensional (3D) acoustic analysis with the time-domain boundary element method (TDBEM). In conventional TDBEM, pair-dependent retarded times couple spatial interactions to historical boundary data, causing substantial storage and history-convolution costs. The proposed representation decouples compressible spatial interactions from propagation history, allowing reuse of the same compressed spatial representation across propagation delays and throughout time marching without additional temporal interpolation of the kernel. For conventional space-time discretizations, blockwise low-rank compression yields the compressed equivalent matrix method in the $\mathcal{H}$-matrix format (CEM-$\mathcal{H}$), with dynamic cluster-pair tracking to skip inactive interactions during wavefront propagation. For low-frequency, long-wavelength problems with a bounded number of nonzero time-lag matrices, the framework is extended to the $\mathcal{H}^2$-matrix format (CEM-$\mathcal{H}^2$) using delay-consistent partitioning, shared coupling matrices, and nested cluster bases. Under sparsity and bounded-parameter assumptions, storage and per-step cost of CEM-$\mathcal{H}^2$ both scale as $O(N_s)$, excluding preprocessing. Numerical results agree well with conventional TDBEM and semi-analytical reference solutions. For CEM-$\mathcal{H}$, the storage requirement for a sphere with $N_s=20,480$ is reduced from approximately 349.0 GB to 1.6 GB, with a speedup of approximately $45.4\times$. For CEM-$\mathcal{H}^2$, simulations with up to $N_s=1,310,720$ are performed in the low-frequency, long-wavelength regime. A million-degree-of-freedom underwater-vehicle model is also analyzed. These results demonstrate the capability of the proposed framework for large-scale 3D transient acoustic analysis using TDBEM.

entries.name: Partitioned iterative FD-SPH for fluid-rigid-body interaction: Stability and validation for lightweight floating bodies
entries.abstract: This study assesses partitioned iterative fictitious-domain smoothed particle hydrodynamics (FD-SPH) for free-surface fluid-rigid-body interaction. Extending a strong-coupling framework for deformable structures, it combines volume-based hydrodynamic loads with Newton-Euler rigid-body updates. Within each time step, the mismatch between pressure-projected fictitious-fluid and rigid-body velocities is fed back iteratively. A fractional-step interpretation identifies conditions under which Passively Moving Solid (PMS) projection and Newton-Euler updates yield identical rigid-body velocities. Single-pass and iterative FD-SPH are compared under matched conditions. A two-dimensional settling-disk benchmark agrees with published results. In three-dimensional buoyancy-driven cube tests, single-pass coupling becomes unstable at specific gravities of 0.1 and 0.2. At 0.1, reducing the time-step size by a factor of 500 does not suppress the instability. Iterative strong coupling remains stable across the tested range of 0.1-1.0. Equilibrium heights and orientations agree with hydrostatic expectations and published stable configurations, respectively. Two- and three-dimensional wet-bed dam-break simulations reproduce experimental trends in wave elevation and floating-body heave and pitch. Two star-shaped rigid bodies demonstrate applicability to complex geometries without explicit interface reconstruction or surface-normal evaluation. All production strong-coupling simulations satisfy the prescribed relative-residual criterion at every time step before reaching the maximum coupling-iteration count. These results support iterative FD-SPH for lightweight and complex floating bodies in transient free-surface flows.

entries.name: On the solution of a question for meromorphic functions sharing three values IM and a fourth value CM in the complex plane
entries.abstract: In 1926, Nevanlinna (Acta Math. {\bf 48} (1926), no. 3-4, 367-391) proved that if two distinct and non-constant meromorphic functions $f$ and $g$ share $a_1,$ $a_2,$ $a_3,$ $a_4$ CM in the complex plane, where $a_1,$ $a_2,$ $a_3,$ $a_4$ are four distinct complex values in the extended complex plane, then $f$ is a Möbius transformation of $g$, two of the shared values, say $a_1$ and $a_2$, are Picard exceptional values, and the cross ratio $\left(a_1, a_2, a_3, a_4\right)=-1.$ Later on, Gundersen (Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. {\bf 277} (1983), no. 2, 545-567. Correction: {\bf 304} (1987), 847-850) proved that if two non-constant meromorphic functions share two values CM and share two other values IM, then the functions share all four values CM. In 1992, Gundersen (Complex Var. Elliptic Equ. {\bf 20} (1992), no. 1-4, 99-106) proposed the following famous question: if two non-constant meromorphic functions share three distinct values IM and share a fourth value CM, then do the functions necessarily share all four values CM? This question is a long-standing question in the studies of the Nevanlinna's value distribution theory of meromorphic functions, and has not been completely resolved by now. In this paper, we completely resolve the question, and prove that if two distinct and non-constant meromorphic functions $f$ and $g$ share $a_1,$ $a_2,$ $a_3$ IM and $\infty$ CM, where $a_1,$ $a_2,$ $a_3$ are three distinct and finite complex values in the complex plane, then $f$ and $g$ also share $a_1,$ $a_2,$ $a_3$ CM.

entries.name: A One-Sided Liouville Theorem and a Critical Sparse-Support Inverse Theorem for Discrete Harmonic Functions
entries.abstract: We answer the one-sided Liouville question of Buhovsky, Logunov, Malinnikova, and Sodin (Duke Math. J. 171 (2022), Remark 1.4). There is an absolute $\varepsilon>0$ such that a real harmonic function on $\mathbb{Z}^2$ is constant if it is nonnegative on at least a $1-\varepsilon$ proportion of every sufficiently large centered square. More generally, for every nonconstant real harmonic function and every $a\le b$, the sets $\{u<a\}$ and $\{u>b\}$ each occupy a fixed positive proportion of the same arbitrarily large centered squares. Turning from sign conditions to sparse supports, we prove in three dimensions a local inverse theorem at the critical quadratic support scale. Write $Q_R=[-R,R]^3\cap\mathbb{Z}^3$. If a complex-valued function is harmonic in $Q_{30R}$ and has at most $AR^2$ nonzero values there, its support in $Q_R$ lies in at most $K_A$ characteristic planes $x_i\pm x_j=c$. The minimum number $m_3(N)$ of nonzero values in $Q_N$ among whole-lattice harmonic functions nonzero at the origin satisfies $m_3(N)=(1+o(1))(2N+1)^2$. More generally, if a fixed nonzero harmonic function on $\mathbb{Z}^3$ has $O(N^2)$ nonzero values in $Q_N$ along a sequence $N\to\infty$, then its support has a unique irredundant cover by finitely many characteristic planes. If there are $k$ such planes, the support count in $Q_N$ is $k(2N+1)^2+O_u(N)$.

entries.name: Parafermi algebra and semiprimality
entries.abstract: The principles of rational parafermi algebra of Mersenne order $p=2^n-1$, developed in an earlier work, are recapitulated in the introduction: A Continued Kronecker Square-root process (CKS) dispenses with irrational numbers.The process creates two types of lower triangular square matrices, called of $G$-type and $J$-type, whose elements decompose Catalan numbers in particular ways. Trilinear relations, which have the lower-left matrix part interact with a suitably chosen block-diagonal part, are only semi-conservative in that $G$-type and $J$-type elements are preserved but appear in an operational context showing different direction of rotation. The second section begins with an examination of the immersion effect, a tendency of LL$(G_{μ,ν}^{(p')})$ (for $G$-like lower-left part at order $p'\hspace*{-0.8mm}:=2^{n+1}\hspace*{-0.5mm}-\hspace*{-0.5mm}1$) to adopt pecularities of LL$(J_{μ,ν}^{(p)})$: a semiprime in LL$(J_{μ,ν}^{(15)})$ leads to a semiprime in LL$(G_{μ,ν}^{(31)})$; diagonally repeated semiprimes in LL$(J_{μ,ν}^{(31)})$ prompt diagonally repeated semiprimes in LL$(G_{μ,ν}^{(63)})$. After translating opposing directions of rotation to differently directed paths that emerge when the ordinal number of the second factor of a semiprime with first factor 3, 7 or 11 is varied, a rulebook is formulated which reveals that paths associated with LL$(J_{μ,ν}^{(p)})$ are not only aimed differently; they occur five times as often as paths associated with LL$(G_{μ,ν}^{(p)})$. The coincidence of the frequency ratio ${\cal G}^{(p)}/{\cal J}^{(p)}$ with the mass ratio of conventional matter over dark matter is commented upon at the close.

entries.name: Schubert Calculus in the Eye of the Storm
entries.abstract: We introduce new combinatorial objects, called storm diagrams, to study the torus-equivariant quantum $K$-theory of complete flag varieties $GL_n(\mathbb{C})/B$. We consider the quantum product of an arbitrary Schubert class with a modified Hirzebruch $λ_y$-class of a tautological subbundle. We show that its Schubert expansion coefficients are given by the total weights of storm diagrams. As applications, we establish Pieri rules for the torus-equivariant quantum $K$-theory of partial flag varieties $GL_n(\mathbb{C})/P$. Our storm diagrams provide the first combinatorial model for a manifestly positive multiplication formula for partial flag varieties beyond the Chevalley case, with restrictions imposed on only one of the two Schubert classes.

entries.name: Optimal long-time derivative estimates for underdamped Langevin dynamics
entries.abstract: We study the long-time behaviour of derivatives of the semigroup $P_t=e^{t\mathcal{A}}$ generated by the underdamped Langevin (kinetic Fokker-Planck) operator $\mathcal{A}$ on $L^2(μ)$, where the Gibbs measure $μ$ is not required to be finite. Under a weighted relative bound on the Hessian of the potential, we prove that for every integer $m\ge 0$ the squared $L^2(μ)$ norms of $\mathcal{A}^m P_t h_0$ and of $\nabla_{x,v}\mathcal{A}^m P_t h_0$ are bounded by $C_m t^{-2m}\|h_0\|^2$ and $D_m t^{-(2m+1)}\|h_0\|^2$ respectively for large times, and the free dynamics shows that these exponents are optimal. The proof rests on a resolvent estimate near the imaginary axis, valid for every smooth potential, which follows from the adjoint relation between the generator and the velocity reversal and from the Gaussian Poincaré inequality in the velocity variable.

entries.name: PWLNet: A Framework for Linearized Neural Surrogates in Nonlinear Process Optimization
entries.abstract: Neural networks represent nonlinear process systems accurately, but embedding them in optimization is difficult because smooth activations introduce nonlinear, nonconvex constraints. PWLNet is a Python framework for building optimization-compatible neural surrogates through exact and piecewise-linear reformulations. It combines baseline and physics-informed training, optimization-aware pruning, and Pyomo embeddings based on ReLU mixed-integer linear models, exact tanh nonlinear models, PWL-tanh formulations, and binary-free SOSX branch-and-LP. PWL-native training uses the same activation in training and embedding, avoiding extra linearization error. It is evaluated on Boston housing, the Williams-Otto process, the Van de Vusse reactor, and a hydroformylation semi-batch reactor. On Boston housing, SOSX training gave the best common-architecture model (test MAE 1.984, R2 = 0.925). On Williams-Otto, pruning 15% of hidden neurons reduced MILP solution time 6.5-fold while preserving the selected operating point. For the Van de Vusse reactor, a physics-informed ReLU RNN pruned from 32 to 12 hidden units enabled tractable exact MILP embedding and a 4% true-plant economic gain over the best ramp-and-hold policy, while terminal-aware shrinking-horizon prediction reached 99.7% of the direct-shooting reference. For the hydroformylation reactor, one-step exact-tanh IPOPT reached 99.2% of the certified reference product with peak pressure 20.002 bar (limit 20 bar) and 14.36 s total solve time over 280 moves; ReLU and PWL-native controllers achieved comparable recovery, with ReLU fastest. Longer horizons and physics-informed training did not consistently improve closed-loop results. Overall, compact linearized neural surrogates enable accurate, tractable optimization in steady-state and dynamic applications, with constraint fidelity identified as a key direction for improvement.

entries.name: A note on a nonlocal antisymmetric barrier
entries.abstract: In this note, we present a barrier function for an equation involving the fractional Laplacian in the antisymmetric setting, providing an explicit inequality in the full positivity set of the function. This leads to an improvement of the quantitative maximum principle given in [DPTV26], where the bound was obtained in a strict subset of its positivity set and required additional assumptions on lower order coefficients. As a consequence of this, we give an optimal lower bound on the growth of antisymmetric solutions from the symmetry hyperplane.

entries.name: Proof of Stanley's Conjecture on the Leading Ehrhart Coefficients of the Birkhoff Polytope
entries.abstract: Let $c(n,k)$ denote the coefficient of $r^{(n-1)^2-k}$ in the Ehrhart polynomial of the $n\times n$ Birkhoff polytope. For every fixed nonnegative integer $k$, we prove that $c(n,k)/c(n,0)\sim n^{3k}/(2^k k!)$ as $n\to\infty$, confirming a conjecture of Stanley.

entries.name: Uniform Bounds of $F$-Signature and Effective Ideal Containments
entries.abstract: We establish inequalities between numerical invariants and ideal containments in local rings containing a field. We prove the positivity of $F$-signature for klt-type algebras essentially of finite type over $\mathbb{C}$ under prime characteristic reduction and resolve the Uniform Symbolic Topology Problem effectively for both $F$-finite strongly $F$-regular rings of prime characteristic and klt type algebras over $\mathbb{C}$. Consequently, letting $s(R)$ denote the $F$-signature and $d$ the Krull dimension, if $d\geq 2$ then $I^{\left(\left\lceil\frac{d-1}{s(R)}\right\rceil n\right)} \subseteq \overline{I^{n}}$ and $I^{\left(d\left\lceil\frac{d-1}{s(R)}\right\rceil n\right)} \subseteq I^n$ for every ideal $I \subseteq R$ and $n \in \mathbb{N}$ in these settings.

entries.name: $p$-adic Fourier theory for unramified extensions of $\mathbb{Q}_p$ and weighted Monna maps
entries.abstract: We generalize a recent result of Ardakov and Berger on the $p$-adic valuations of Schneider--Teitelbaum polynomials evaluated at Lubin--Tate periods over the unramified quadratic extension of $\mathbb{Q}_p$. For finite unramified extensions of $\mathbb{Q}_p$ of degree $f \geq 2$, we introduce a weighted analogue of the Monna map and show that it determines the valuations of these polynomial values for Lubin--Tate formal groups whose formal logarithms are $p$-typical. Our proof uses the Artin--Hasse exponential and Witt vectors. As an application, for a distinguished Lubin--Tate formal group, we determine the exact norms of the associated Schneider--Teitelbaum polynomials on Banach spaces of locally analytic functions and obtain an explicit rescaling of the Banach basis constructed by Bannai and Kobayashi so that each basis element has norm one.

entries.name: Two Knuth orbits of order 256 without primitive semifield coordinatizations
entries.abstract: We exhibit two Knuth orbits of semifield planes of order 256 in which every coordinatizing semifield is nonprimitive on both the left and the right. Each orbit consists of two isotopy classes. The first orbit contains 168 isomorphism classes of unital semifields and the second contains 32. We give binary multiplication matrices for a representative of each orbit and an exhaustive computation that verifies nonprimitivity and the counts directly from these matrices.

entries.name: The Csisz{á}r order for ranking the importance of input random variables
entries.abstract: Csisz{á}r indices $S\_f(X,Y)$, defined as the $f$-divergence between the joint distribution of a general random couple $(X,Y)$ and the product of its marginal distributions, are widely used to quantify dependence between the input variable $X$ and the output variable $Y$. We show that the ranking of two input variables $X$ and $X'$ in terms of their importance w.r.t.\ the output variable, given by the comparison of the Csisz{á}r indices $S\_f(X,Y)$ and $S\_f(X',Y)$ depends on the choice of $f$. We introduce the Csisz{á}r order of input variables as the uniform ordering of Csisz{á}r indices over all proper convex functions $f$. We give a sufficient condition to prove Csiszár order of two input multivariate random variables. We fully characterize it in two cases: when $(X,X',Y)$ is a Gaussian vector (in the one-dimensional case this amount to compare the square of their correlation); and when $X$, $X'$ and $Y$ are Bernoulli random variables. Finally, motivated by sensitivity analysis, we show that, when $(X,X',Y)$ is a three-dimensional Gaussian random vector, thresholding $X$, $X'$, and $Y$ either preserves the Csisz{á}r order or makes the input variables incomparable; in particular thresholding never reverses the ranking.

entries.name: Rational maps with at most three critical values have no Herman rings
entries.abstract: We prove that any rational map with at most three critical values has no Herman rings. This generalizes previous results of Shishikura and Milnor on bi-critical rational maps.

entries.name: Minimal primes and radicality of join-meet ideals of modular lattices with one diamond
entries.abstract: Let $L$ be a finite modular lattice with exactly one diamond, that is, exactly one interval of length two with at least three atoms. We describe the minimal primes of the join-meet ideal $I_L$ in terms of maximal closed distributive sublattices of $L$, and we show that $I_L$ has height $|L|-\mathrm{rank}(L)$. Moreover, we characterize the radicality of $I_L$, over any field, in terms of the complements of the atoms of the diamond in their fibres. Finally, we prove that $I_L$ is unmixed if and only if all its minimal primes have the same height, if and only if the rank of every maximal closed distributive sublattice through an atom of the diamond is $\mathrm{rank}(L)-1$; in this case $I_L$ is radical.

entries.name: A family of homogeneous convex non-scattering domains with analytic non-circular boundaries
entries.abstract: A homogeneous planar non-scattering domain is a bounded medium with a constant material coefficient that produces no scattered field for some nonzero entire solution of the Helmholtz equation at a particular wave number. It is known that the boundary of such a domain must be real analytic at all points where the incident field does not vanish. Previously, disks were the only known examples. We construct a family of homogeneous strictly convex non-scattering domains that are neither disks nor ellipses. The family bifurcates from a particular non-scattering disk, with the boundary, wave number, and constant coefficient varying along the branch. The construction uses a conformal change of variables and analytic bifurcation theory applied to the resulting nonlinear problem.

entries.name: Moduli spaces of $(3,6)$-$K3$ surfaces and cubic surfaces
entries.abstract: We compare the ball quotient for marked nodal cubic surfaces with the arithmetic quotient of a domain of type IV associated with $K3$ surfaces arising from configurations of six lines in $\mathbb{P}^2$. Using the Coble map and the period mapping associated with the hypergeometric system of type $(3,6)$, we identify a common open subset of the GIT quotient of six ordered points in $\mathbb{P}^2$ and the ball quotient. This identification gives an analog in dimension four of the Janus-like phenomenon for the Segre cubic and the Igusa quartic, making precise a comparison suggested by Allcock, Carlson, and Toledo. For a related family of lattice-polarized $K3$ surfaces, we give a geometric realization of the ring of meromorphic modular forms with prescribed poles and trivial character and describe the corresponding Looijenga compactification.

entries.name: Critical nonlocal GJMS operator on odd dimensional spheres and mean field equation
entries.abstract: For a smooth axially symmetric function on $\mathbb{S}^n$ with $n\geq 1$, in odd dimensions we prove a neat formula for the critical nonlocal GJMS operator $P_n$ similar to the one in even dimensions. With this formula, we give a simple proof of the Liouville theorem by Gui-Hu-Xie (J. Funct. Anal. 2022): Every smooth axially symmetric solution to $$\frac{1}{n+1} P_n u = (n-1)!(e^{nu}-1) \quad \mathrm{on} \quad \mathbb{S}^n,n\geq 2$$ is identically zero, without using any delicate property of Gegenbauer polynomials.

entries.name: High-Order Area-Preserving Runge--Kutta Methods for Surface Diffusion Flow of Curves
entries.abstract: We propose a class of high-order area-preserving Runge--Kutta (RK) methods for the surface diffusion flow of curves, a curvature-driven geometric flow that decreases the perimeter while conserving the enclosed area. By coupling the parametric finite element approximation of the classical BGN formulation with symplectic RK time discretisation, we rigorously prove that the fully discrete scheme unconditionally conserves the enclosed area of curves. This conservation arises solely from the intrinsic symplectic structure of the RK methods, without introducing any additional constraints, auxiliary variables, or Lagrange multipliers to enforce structure preservation. To attain high temporal accuracy, we adopt $q$-stage Gauss RK methods, which are symplectic and yield order $2q$ (e.g., $q=1,2,3$). The resulting fully implicit, strongly nonlinear system is solved efficiently via an equivalent discrete formulation combined with a monolithic damped Newton iteration. Extensive numerical tests on various evolving curves validate the theoretical findings, confirming exact area preservation, high-order temporal convergence, and favorable mesh quality, while the Newton iteration count rapidly decreases to fewer than 8 per step, demonstrating the robustness of the tailored solver.

entries.name: The construction of a regular non-Berwald Landsberg surface
entries.abstract: We construct a regular non-Berwald Landsberg metric of zero flag curvature on an open subset of the plane via a periodically forced oscillator equation. We solve the associated return equation exactly to obtain closed, strongly convex coindicatrices. Starting from a finite truncation of a formal control, we use a uniform local inverse for a periodic comparison operator and a smoothing iteration to make the return map of the original oscillator equal to the identity on the chosen base neighborhood. A direct calculation of the spray exhibits a nonzero component of the Berwald tensor.

entries.name: Conditional propagation of chaos for systems of particles with polynomial interactions
entries.abstract: We consider N interacting particles taking values in the real numbers and evolving in discrete time with time step 1/n. Each particle follows an individual dynamics, driven by its own noise, which depends on the total configuration via a polynomial interaction. Moreover, all particles receive the same collective perturbation. This perturbation is given by a multilinear homogeneous sum of order $ m \geq 2$ of independent centered random fields which are evaluated at the current positions of the particles. We show that, as N and n tend to infinity, the system converges to the solution of a conditional McKean-Vlasov equation which is driven by an additional Brownian motion which emerges in the limit from the collective perturbations. Moreover we give explicit bounds for the Wasserstein-2-distance. Our proof combines the invariance principle of Mossel, O'Donnell and Oleszkiewicz (2010), the CLT for Wiener chaoses in the Wasserstein-2-form of Ledoux, Nourdin and Peccati (2015) and a conditional law of large numbers for weighted U-statistics proven in this paper.

entries.name: On the contact of regular surfaces in $\mathbb{R}^4$ with toroidal cylinders and their apparent contours
entries.abstract: We study the contact of regular surfaces in $\mathbb{R}^4$ with toroidal cylinders $S^1(r) \times \mathbb{R}^2$. We relate the contact type to the singularities of the corresponding parallel projections along the direction of the axes of the toroidal cylinders, the geometry of the apparent contours under these projections, and the geometry of the original surfaces.

entries.name: On the dimension of $V$-variable fractals
entries.abstract: Random recursive sets have been used to model a wide range of fractal phenomena, but they can be slow and difficult to generate. $V$-variability address this problem by allowing these sets at most $V$ distinct shapes at each level of magnification. The formulae for the almost sure Hausdorff dimension of both classes is known, and it has been conjectured that (under mild assumptions) the $V$-variable dimension converges to the random recursive dimension as $V\to\infty$. We prove this conjecture.

entries.name: Stars and paths in oriented graphs
entries.abstract: Let $\overrightarrow{F}$ be a fixed oriented graph. Its oriented Turán number, written $\exo(n,\overrightarrow{F})$, is the largest size of an $n$-vertex oriented graph with no copy of $\overrightarrow{F}$. This parameter extends the classical notion of Turán number to oriented graphs. In this paper, we investigate the supersaturation results for the directed path $P_k~(k\geq 2)$ and all oriented stars $\overrightarrow{S}_{p,q}~(0\leq p\leq q$), and all oriented paths of order at most four.

entries.name: An improved Moore bound for girths seven and eleven
entries.abstract: Let $n(d,k)$ be the minimum number of vertices of a graph of minimum degree $d$ and girth at least $g=2k+1$. A simple counting argument gives the classical lower bound $n(d,k)\ge m(d,k)=1+d\sum_{i=0}^{k-1}(d-1)^i$, known as the Moore bound and dating back at least to 1960. Apart from complete graphs and odd cycles, graphs attaining this lower bound can exist only for girth $5$ and degrees $3,7$ and $57$ (Hoffman and Singleton 1960; Bannai and Ito 1973; Damerell 1973). Nevertheless, for more than sixty years this lower bound has not been substantially improved beyond an additive constant. For $k\geq 3$, i.e. girth at least $7$, the best general bound was $n(d,k)\ge m(d,k)+2$, due to Bannai and Ito (1981). We show that for fixed girth $7$ and growing degree $d$ we have $n(d,3)\ge m(d,3)+(1-o(1))d/8$. Furthermore, for girth $11$ we have $n(d,5)\ge m(d,5)+Ω(d^{3/5})$. In particular, the excess $n(d,k)-m(d,k)$, for $k\in\{3,5\}$, tends to infinity with $d$ and is therefore generally unbounded, which answers a question of Bollobás from 1978. For the degree/diameter problem we obtain similar bounds. A graph of maximum degree $d$ and diameter $3$ or $5$ has at most $m(d,3)-Ω(\sqrt{d})$ or $m(d,5)-Ω(d^{3/10})$ vertices, respectively. This answers a question of Bermond and Bollobás from 1981: for every constant $c$ there are $d$ and $k$ such that every graph of maximum degree $d$ and diameter $k$ has at least $c$ fewer vertices than the Moore bound.

entries.name: Optimal Beurling-Hörmander-type uncertainty principles and nontriviality of Gelfand-Shilov spaces
entries.abstract: We study how rapidly a nonzero function $f \in L^2(\mathbb{R})$ and its Fourier transform $\widehat{f}$ can simultaneously decay. For each suitable weight function $ω$, we construct a convex weight function $\varpi$ and establish the existence of a threshold $Φ_{(ω,\varpi^*)} \in (0, \infty)$, where $\varpi^*$ denotes the convex conjugate of $\varpi$. For $a,b > 0$, the conditions \[ \int_{-\infty}^\infty |f(x)| e^{ω(a|x|)} \, \mathrm{d}x < \infty \qquad \text{and} \qquad \int_{-\infty}^\infty |\widehat{f}(ξ)| e^{\varpi^*(b|ξ|)} \, \mathrm{d}ξ < \infty \] force $f = 0$ when $ab > Φ_{(ω,\varpi^*)}$, whereas the functions satisfying both conditions form a dense subspace of $L^2(\mathbb{R})$ when $ab < Φ_{(ω,\varpi^*)}$. Similar results are also established in higher dimensions. We characterize the weights $ω$ for which $\varpi$ is equivalent to $ω$ and use this to determine when the Beurling-Hörmander uncertainty principle is optimal. A discrete form of the same construction yields a characterization of the nontriviality of Gelfand-Shilov spaces $\mathcal{S}^{M}_{A}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ and $Σ^{M}_{A}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ in terms of their defining weight sequences $M$ and $A$, under suitable regularity assumptions.

entries.name: Sharp minimax rates and adaptive estimation of latent proportions in bivariate Poisson mixtures
entries.abstract: We study estimation of the mean latent composition in a bivariate Poisson mixture. Conditional on an unobserved intensity S and proportion U, two counts are independent Poisson variables with respective means SU and S(1-U). The mixing law is unrestricted on the Cartesian product [a,b] x [0,1], where a and b are finite constants satisfying 0 < a < b, and dependence between S and U is allowed. Although the mixing distribution is identifiable, the usual ratio of mean counts estimates an intensity-weighted proportion and may be biased for theta = E[U]. We construct polynomial estimators based on factorial moments and establish the exact leading exponent of the minimax squared-error risk on the logarithmic scale, without claiming an exact multiplicative minimax constant. We also derive the sharp logarithmic separation exponent for testing zero latent covariance and construct an adaptive estimator achieving parametric squared-error risk on the zero-covariance submodel while retaining the optimal full-model logarithmic minimax exponent. Simulations illustrate the bias-variance trade-off, the role of polynomial regularization, and the distinction between theoretically guaranteed and empirically calibrated adaptation.

entries.name: A variational theory for von Kármán vortex streets
entries.abstract: We construct von Kármán vortex streets as global kinetic energy maximizers for the 2D Euler flow in an infinite periodic channel: our variational framework imposes no a prior symmetry, support constraints, or sign conditions on the admissible class. More specifically, under $O(\varepsilon^{-2})$ constraint of the absolute vorticity maximum with other natural constraints, we show that the maximizers are traveling pairs of simply connected vortex patches of support radius $O(\varepsilon)$, converging to the von Kármán point-vortex configuration satisfying glide reflection symmetry as $\varepsilon \to 0$. We prove nonlinear stability of the von Kármán streets under a bound on the vertical support, using a compactness result valid for more general assumptions. Furthermore, we construct slightly tilted asymmetric von Kármán vortex streets as energy maximizers under a tilted moment constraint.

entries.name: Notes on modules of finite injective dimension
entries.abstract: Motivated by Bass' conjecture, we study finitely generated modules of finite injective dimension and the additional constraints they impose on the ambient ring. Beyond ensuring the Cohen--Macaulay property, the presence of such modules enforces further conditions on the ring, including reducedness, normality, being an integral domain, and various singularity conditions such as complete intersection, Gorenstein, and beyond. This continues to detect non-singularity as well. We also address the reflexivity (and also torsionlessness) of modules with finite injective dimension and show that this forces the ring to be quasi-normal. In the same vein, we investigate the injective dimension of tensor products and endomorphism rings. Finally, we study the behavior of R when high syzygies of ksurject onto a non-zero R-module of finite injective dimension.

entries.name: An analogue of Reed's conjecture for digraphs
entries.abstract: Reed in 1998 conjectured that every graph $G$ satisfies $χ(G) \leq \lceil \frac{Δ(G)+1+ω(G)}{2} \rceil$. As a partial result, he proved the existence of $\varepsilon > 0$ for which every graph $G$ satisfies $χ(G) \leq \lceil (1-\varepsilon)(Δ(G)+1)+\varepsilonω(G) \rceil$. We propose an analogue conjecture for digraphs. Given a digraph $D$, we denote by $\vecχ(D)$ the dichromatic number of $D$, which is the minimum number of colours needed to partition $D$ into acyclic induced subdigraphs. We let $\overleftrightarrowω(D)$ denote the size of the largest biclique (a set of vertices inducing a complete digraph) of $D$ and $\tildeΔ(D) = \max_{v\in V(D)} \sqrt{d^+(v) \cdot d^-(v)}$. We conjecture that every digraph $D$ satisfies $\vecχ(D) \leq \lceil \frac{\tildeΔ(D)+1+\overleftrightarrowω(D)}{2} \rceil$, which if true implies Reed's conjecture. As a partial result, we prove the existence of $\varepsilon >0$ for which every digraph $D$ satisfies $\vecχ(D) \leq \lceil (1-\varepsilon)(\tildeΔ(D)+1)+\varepsilon\overleftrightarrowω(D) \rceil$. This implies both Reed's result and an independent result of Harutyunyan and Mohar for oriented graphs. To obtain this upper bound on $\vecχ$, we prove that every digraph $D$ with $\overleftrightarrowω(D) > \frac{2}{3}(Δ_{\max}(D)+1)$, where $Δ_{\max}(D) = \max_{v\in V(D)} \max(d^+(v),d^-(v))$, admits an acyclic set of vertices intersecting each biclique of $D$, which generalises a result of King. We finally give a short proof that every oriented graph $D$ with underlying graph $G$ satisfies $\vecχ(D) \leq \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} \tildeΔ(D) + 2$ and $\vecχ(D) \leq \frac{1}{3}Δ(G)+2$, improving on results of Golowich and Steiner, respectively.

entries.name: Unimodality and Cluster Algebras from Surfaces
entries.abstract: We prove that the rank polynomial of the lattice of order ideals of a loop fence poset is unimodal. This poset arises as the poset of join-irreducibles in the lattice of good matchings of loop graphs associated with notched arcs. Equivalently, such polynomials can be obtained by evaluating all coefficient variables in an F-polynomial at a single variable q. We also conclude that the rank polynomial of any tagged arc, whether plain or notched, is not only unimodal but also satisfies a symmetry condition known as almost interlacing. Furthermore, when the lamination consists of a single curve, the cluster expansion-evaluated by setting all cluster variables to 1 and all coefficient variables to q-is also unimodal. We conjecture that polynomials in this case are log-concave.

entries.name: A nonvanishing criterion and families of counterexamples to the motivic Peterson conjecture
entries.abstract: The motivic Peterson conjecture asks whether the numerical condition forcing classical polynomial indecomposables to vanish has the same consequence in motivic cohomology. Kameko disproved this assertion by constructing a family of non-hit monomials. To determine all linear relations among the projected classes of these monomials, we compute the image of the motivic hit subspace under a projection onto their span: it consists precisely of the combinations whose coefficients sum to zero. Explicit Bockstein preimages establish the reverse inclusion, showing that no further linear relations hold and yielding a nonvanishing criterion. A binary calculation then produces infinitely many counterexamples for each fixed difference of at least three between the number of variables and the exterior degree.

entries.name: Wedge Sampling: Efficient Tensor Completion with Nearly-Linear Sample Complexity
entries.abstract: We introduce wedge sampling, a non-adaptive sampling scheme for recovering an order-$k$ low-rank tensor of side length $n$ from structured observations of its entries. The scheme samples pairs of entries in the same column of a tensor unfolding, forming length-two paths (wedges) in the associated bipartite sampling graph. The products of the paired entries supply the row correlations needed for spectral initialization in regimes where uniform sampling yields too few wedges. For fixed rank, incoherence, tensor order, and condition number, wedge sampling enables polynomial-time recovery with nearly linear sample complexity in $n$. The spectral initializer can be combined with existing refinement procedures using only an additional $\tilde O(n)$ uniformly sampled entries. Spectral refinement achieves weak recovery to any fixed relative Frobenius error. For symmetric third-order tensors with incoherent canonical polyadic factors, gradient descent achieves exact recovery in the noiseless setting, with error decreasing geometrically. The improvement over the $\tilde O(n^{k/2})$ sample complexity typical of efficient methods under uniform entry sampling shows how the conjectured computational barrier depends on the observation model. A key ingredient for the gradient descent analysis is a concentration bound for sparse random tensors in an incoherent spectral norm. We also give error bounds for both procedures under additive Gaussian noise and explicit signal-to-noise conditions. Beyond tensor completion, the same sampling scheme improves the sample complexity of one-sided matrix completion, where the goal is to recover the left singular subspace of a matrix with many more columns than rows.

entries.name: Cohen-Macaulay squarefree powers of edge ideals of very well-covered graphs
entries.abstract: Let $G$ be a graph with edge ideal $I(G)$. For $q\ge 1$, the $q$th squarefree power $I(G)^{[q]}$ is the Stanley-Reisner ideal of the $q$-matching-free complex $\mathsf{MF}^q(G)$, whose faces are the vertex sets containing no $q$ pairwise disjoint edges. We determine exactly which squarefree powers of the edge ideal of a very well-covered graph are Cohen-Macaulay: if $G$ has $2n$ vertices, then $R/I(G)^{[q]}$ is Cohen-Macaulay if and only if $q=n$, or $q=1$ and $G$ is Cohen-Macaulay, or $G=W(H)$ is a whisker graph and $q \le \left\lfloor \frac{\operatorname{girth}(H)}{2} \right\rfloor$. The answer is independent of the field. The proof rests on a rigidity theorem: among very well-covered graphs, only whisker graphs have a sequentially Cohen-Macaulay squarefree power strictly between the first and the last. For whisker graphs we show that $\mathsf{MF}^q(W(H))$ is vertex decomposable for $q \le \left\lceil \frac{\operatorname{girth}(H)}{2} \right\rceil$, and we express the depth and the regularity of every squarefree power through the homology of explicit auxiliary complexes. As a consequence we prove a conjecture of Das, Roy and Saha on the depth of squarefree powers of whisker cycles. Finally, for every graph with a perfect matching, we compute the top homology of $\mathsf{MF}^q(G)$ and determine when the regularity of $R/I(G)^{[q]}$ attains its maximal possible value.

entries.name: Oort's conjecture on automorphisms of generic supersingular abelian varieties
entries.abstract: We prove Oort's conjecture that generically on the supersingular locus of the moduli space of principally polarized abelian varieties of genus g and in characteristic p, the automorphism group of the universal principally polarized abelian variety consists only of $\pm 1$, unless g=2, 3 or 4 and p=2. On the way, we provide an explicit description of the a=1-locus in the Rapoport-Zink space of principally polarized supersingular p-divisible groups of any dimension g. We also prove analogous results for generic automorphism groups on moduli spaces of supersingular p-divisible groups with and without polarization.

entries.name: The Bollobás--Nikiforov inequality for complete multipartite graphs, with remarks on the $K_4$-free case
entries.abstract: Bollobás and Nikiforov conjectured that every graph $G \neq K_n$ with $m$ edges and clique number $ω$ satisfies $λ_1^2(G) + λ_2^2(G) \leq 2(1 - 1/ω)m$, where $λ_1(G) \geq λ_2(G)$ are the two largest adjacency eigenvalues. We give a short self-contained proof of the inequality for complete multipartite graphs, based on a quadratic-form identity which shows that $λ_2 \leq 0$, and we determine the equality cases in this class. We show that equality in the conjecture is attained by a wider family than the Turán graphs, namely by disjoint unions of two complete bipartite graphs, or of two balanced complete $r$-partite graphs of possibly different orders. For $K_4$-free graphs we record the cases that follow from known results, with corrected attributions, and we give examples showing that three natural lines of attack fail: a Hoffman-type eigenvalue bound for graphs with large independence number, a spectral stability statement for connected graphs, and Zykov symmetrization in an arbitrary direction.

entries.name: Noncommutative Geometry, Spectral Asymptotics, and Semiclassical Analysis, I. Main Results
entries.abstract: In this paper, we combine techniques from functional analysis and spectral theory to obtain semiclassical Weyl laws and extensions of Connes' integration formula for a large class of spectral triples. These results generalize and simplify recent work of McDonald--Sukochev--Zanin: all regularity assumptions and dimension restrictions are removed, and their Tauberian condition is replaced by a weaker spectral condition, Condition~(W), which holds in far greater generality. We also establish Tauberian criteria for Condition~(W) involving zeta functions and heat traces, as sought by Alain Connes. The results are illustrated on bounded Euclidean domains, closed Riemannian manifolds, the Steklov problem, and quantum tori. In the latter setting they resolve a conjecture of Edward McDonald and the author. This is the first part of a two-part work. The proofs of the main technical results are given in Part II.

entries.name: Thresholds for the Frankl-Wang $3/7$ conjecture on maximum-degree ratios
entries.abstract: Let $\mathcal{F}\subset\binom{[n]}{k}$ be an intersecting family, $Δ(\mathcal{F})=\max_{x\in[n]}|\{F\in\mathcal{F}:x\in F\}|$, and $\varrho(\mathcal{F})=Δ(\mathcal{F})/|\mathcal{F}|$. Frankl and Wang conjectured that if $n>100k$ and $|\mathcal{F}|>\binom{n-3}{k-3}$, then $\varrho(\mathcal{F})\ge 3/7$; the constant $3/7$ is sharp because of the Fano-plane construction. In this note we obtain three results. First, we show that no linear threshold $n>Ck$ can be sufficient: using a truncated Fano-plane construction we exhibit, for every constant $C$ and all large $k$, an intersecting family with $n>Ck$, $|\mathcal{F}|>\binom{n-3}{k-3}$, yet $\varrho(\mathcal{F})<3/7$. In particular, the original condition $n>100k$ does not guarantee the conclusion. Second, for $k=3$ we prove that $\varrho(\mathcal{F})\ge 3/7$ holds for every nonempty intersecting $3$-uniform family; the proof is nontrivial and does not rely on any assumption on $n$ or $|\mathcal{F}|$. Third, using the classical pseudo-sunflower bound $|\mathcal{F}|\le t^k$ (for families containing no pseudo-sunflower of size $t+1$), we obtain a completely explicit polynomial threshold for all $k\ge4$: if $n>(k-3)(7k^4+k)+3$ and $|\mathcal{F}|>\binom{n-3}{k-3}$, then $\varrho(\mathcal{F})\ge 3/7$. In particular, the simplified bound $n>7k^5$ is sufficient for every $k\ge4$.

entries.name: At least seven modes in a heteroscedastic three-component bivariate Gaussian mixture
entries.abstract: A Gaussian mixture density can have more modes than components. It has been conjectured that the maximum number of modes of a $d$-variate $k$-component Gaussian mixture density is $\binom{d+k-1}{d}$, which equals six for $(d,k)=(2,3)$. We construct an explicit family of equally weighted heteroscedastic three-component bivariate Gaussian mixture densities with at least seven distinct nondegenerate modes, showing that this conjectured upper bound fails for $(d,k)=(2,3)$. To the best of our knowledge, this provides the first counterexample to the conjecture across all pairs $(d,k)$.

entries.name: Weighted bond posets and a new chromatic symmetric function
entries.abstract: The classical bond lattice of a graph was used in a formula of Whitney to compute the chromatic polynomial. In this paper, we use weighted versions of the bond lattice, to introduce and study a new polynomial and a new symmetric function invariant of a graph.
